criteria.reasoning: The report calls her "Founder and president of Emerson Collective" and "the widow of Apple co-founder Steve Jobs", who "died on October 5, 2011." It states "The fortune was inherited, mostly as Apple and Disney shares."

It describes Emerson Collective as "an LLC that combines grant-making, venture investing and advocacy" and says "Emerson Collective: LLC, not a foundation. It has no Form 990 and no public grant list." Nothing in the report contradicts this.

"Waverley Street Foundation: her climate foundation. It is a 501(c)(3) private foundation (EIN 81-3242506), organized in 2016 as the Emerson Collective Foundation." It says she "committed $3.5 billion over ten years" in a spend-down and that the foundation "funds climate work only."
"Emerson Collective agreed to buy a majority stake in July 2017", and her current roles include "majority investor and board chair of The Atlantic."
"The Atlantic, which she controls, is headquartered in Washington, D.C." The report also notes that "College Track Southeast D.C. (Ward 8) opened in January 2020."
It gives "$13.9 billion (Forbes real time, April 25, 2026)" and advises "Use about $12–14 billion". It labels the older $19–20 billion figures as superseded.
"She sold her stake in December 2025 to the Qatar Investment Authority and Arctos Partners, at a reported $7.2 billion enterprise value... It is no longer a holding."

The report names several journalism grantees with documented amounts: ProPublica $500,000 (2016), $700,000 (2017) and $4.6 million over three years; The Texas Tribune $350,000 a year; Chalkbeat $200,000–$300,000 a year; The 19th $100,000 (2020); The Current $170,000 over two years; and "about $37 million" in total. All of them match.

On The Atlantic it says "This is a for-profit investment, not a gift", and it lists Axios, The Athletic, Ozy and Pop-Up as "Other media investments (all for-profit)." None of these is added into the giving totals.
"Emerson Collective does not accept unsolicited submissions of any kind [10]. The only route is a warm introduction."

Strategy step 1 says "Do not send a proposal, letter of inquiry or cold pitch to Emerson Collective or the Waverley Street Foundation". Step 2 is "Build a warm introduction" through grantee newsrooms and the AJP network. No unsolicited submission is recommended anywhere.
"XQ Institute. She co-founded it in 2015 with Russlynn Ali, and she chairs it." Also: "College Track. She co-founded it in 1997." Both founding years are correct.

The ask is "$300,000 over three years ($100,000 a year)". It is anchored explicitly to "The 19th: $100,000", "The Current: $170,000 over two years" and "The Texas Tribune and Chalkbeat: $200,000–$350,000 a year."

Every fact checked agrees with the fact sheet: biography, net-worth figures, the Atlantic stake and price, the Monumental sale, the Waverley Street figures, the founding years and every journalism grant amount. The Atlantic is placed in Washington, D.C. I found no contradiction.
